title: cmdbook — save a command once, run it with one click
excerpt: A desktop app for the commands you run every day. Save them with their prompts, variables and working directory, then run them with one click, from your terminal, on a schedule or from your AI agent.
content_html:
A desktop app for the commands you run every day

Keep each command with its prompts, variables and working directory. Run it with one click, from your terminal, on a schedule or from your AI agent.

macOS 12+ · Windows 10+ · Linux · No account · Your commands stay on your machine

What it does

A few things cmdbook does for you.

Save it once. A command with prompts becomes a form: drop a file, pick an option, and your last answers are remembered. Free

How it fits

Works alongside your terminal. Stays on your computer.

Not a terminal replacement

Keep using your terminal for interactive work. cmdbook keeps the commands you run again and again, and runs them for you.

Not shell history

History remembers what you typed, not which version worked or what to change next time. Why a command library →

Local, and yours

Your commands are stored on your computer and can be exported at any time. The CLI and the local API only accept connections from this computer.

No account

Download and use the Free plan without signing up. Pro needs an activation code, not an account.

Usage statistics you can turn off

cmdbook counts a few actions, such as a command created or run. Never command text, names, paths, output or secrets. It tells you on first launch and sends nothing before that; turn it off in Settings → General → Usage statistics.

Works offline

Commands run without a connection. cmdbook goes online only to activate Pro, to receive new Pro features or renewed updates, and to release a device.

Pricing

The Free plan covers the core command workflow.

Questions

Common questions.

Is cmdbook free?

Yes. The local command library and core workflow are available on the Free plan. Pro adds advanced workflow features and updates during your selected term.

Does cmdbook replace my terminal?

No. Use your normal terminal for interactive work. cmdbook is for commands and scripts you run often and want to start, stop, and find again easily.

Where is my data stored?

Your command library is stored locally on your computer. You decide when to export or connect external services.

Where are the plan details?

Each plan on the pricing card shows its price, how long updates are included and whether it renews. The full rules are in the cmdbook Product Terms.

How many devices can I activate?

Each Pro license covers up to 3 devices. You can release a device and activate another one.

Is cmdbook open source?

No. cmdbook is a commercial app from printf.app, an independent studio. The Free plan has no time limit and needs no account.

What does cmdbook send over the network?

Anonymous usage statistics (counts of a few actions, never your commands or output), which you can turn off; Pro activation and update checks. Your commands are not uploaded. Details are in the Privacy Policy.

What happens when my updates end?

Pro keeps working in the versions released while your updates were included. A later version keeps its Pro features locked until you renew, or you can reinstall a covered version.

Can I get a refund?

Yes, within 7 days of your order. See the Refund Policy.
